thread:
jess: Quick follow-up from the RFC: we ran into a DNS edge case while testing private control plane in a customer VPC.

sasha: which case? curious.

jess: When customers use split-horizon DNS (internal zones resolving to private endpoints) + a shared egress NAT, some control plane callbacks resolve to public IPs and then get hairpinned through NAT. Latency spikes and some cert SAN validation fails intermittently.

mike: ah yeah. that's the classic private DNS + centralized egress problem. The control plane hostname resolves differently depending on whether the resolver is the VPC resolver or the central recursive.

elaine: can you paste the dig output you saw?

jess: sure:
```
; customer-internal-resolver
$ dig cp.redwood.internal +short
10.2.3.5

; central-recursive
$ dig cp.redwood.internal +short
52.24.10.11
```

sasha: and the client sometimes uses the central-recursive IP because of /etc/resolv.conf ordering? or because the shared egress rewrites DNS?

jess: ordering + occasional stub resolver race. Also DHCP renewals during node scale cause short windows where resolution flips.

mike: two obvious options: 1) enforce control plane endpoints to be reachable only over privatelink / interface endpoint (so public IP never used), or 2) keep public IPs but ensure we preserve source IP and avoid hairpin via SNAT in egress path.

elaine: option 1 seems cleaner for security but is heavier for ops (customer needs to create endpoints/subnets). Option 2 cheaper but brittle across many NAT setups.

sasha: another approach: publish dual A records and mandate client-side svc discovery to prefer internal names—e.g., our agent picks the private A when on a customer VPC. That relies on agent-level heuristics though.

jess: true. agent heuristic helped in spike tests, but customers with third-party proxies/proxy auto-config can break heuristics.

mike: long-term we should treat control plane hostnames as single-tenant-private: create per-customer hostnames under customer-managed zones and use privatelink as default. Short-term, we can add an egress-rule to bypass SNAT for CP traffic when egress IP equals a mapped internal destination (calculated via IP prefix list).

elaine: ops question: how do we detect when to create bypass rules automatically vs having a manual onboarding checklist? We don't want to silently change customer NAT behaviour.

sasha: we can default to notify and recommend a one-click flow in console that asks for permission to create egress bypass resources (for Dedicated/Private tiers). For Hosted we can suggest privatelink onboarding.

jess: for rollout: propose 3 phases:
- 1) short-term: agent heuristics + better docs + alerting when resolution diverges (:warning: auto-detect RDATA mismatch) and inc. observable for hairpin rate
- 2) mid-term: egress bypass rules available as opt-in via console automation for Dedicated/Private customers
- 3) long-term: default privatelink/per-customer private hostnames for Private tier; hosted remains shared but with stronger SNAT preservation

mike: sounds reasonable. we should also update our TLS cert issuance: include both private and public SANs while we transition so validation doesn't fail during flip.

elaine: ops note: adding SANs increases cert lifecycle complexity (revocation) but doable. We'll need to update ACME hooks. I'll add an item to infra backlog.

sasha: one more tradeoff: if we push privatelink hard, some customers (on-prem or air-gapped) can't create endpoints. For those, per-customer VPN/peering + local DNS delegation is the path.

jess: agreed — add a separate path in onboarding for on-prem: local DNS delegation + control plane peering. Our docs should show recommended zone layout and example resolver configs.

ops-bot: deploy-bot:reminder: created task #NET-487: "private-dns-split-detection-and-onboard-flow" (assigned to @elaine)

mike: can someone put a quick spike to measure how often hairpin recursion happens across the last 30 days? I want a baseline.

elaine: I'll run the spike next week and post numbers here. Also adding an alert when SAN mismatch occurs during control plane handshake.

jess: thanks team. I'll draft the RFC follow-up with the 3-phase rollout and link this thread. cc @sasha for the console UX text.

sasha: happy to help with console copy. :thumbsup:

mike: sweet. if we keep phased approach we avoid forcing customers to change overnight.

elaine: ack, will report back Thursday with numbers.

jess: closing loop once infra task lands. thanks!
